Hi Karthik —

Thanks for taking this on. We’re preparing for a private deployment in our AWS account (us-west-2) and need a short architecture + network gate review before kicking off the infra team. High level constraints:
- All traffic to the inference cluster must traverse our transit gateway and go through managed NGFW (no public IPs on host NICs).
- KMS/HSM integration is required for model key wrapping; customer-managed key, offline rotation policy.
- Expected peak concurrency: ~120 qps across 50ms p50 inference responses (model: redwood/7b-optimized).

I attached our internal network requirements spreadsheet (atlas_network_requirements.xlsx).

Can we run through a checklist and sign off on the minimal set of required security controls and firewall rules? Also need a short list of port/peerings we will request from our cloud team for the ticket.

We’re hoping to have the network ticket raised by Monday and a kickoff the following week.

Regards,
Diane Brooks
Director, Platform Engineering
Atlas Health

Diane — thanks for the note and the spreadsheet. I reviewed the requirements and sketched a minimal gate checklist and port matrix so your cloud/network team can raise the ticket with the right details. See the attached: redwood-network-checklist.pdf and infra-diagram.png.

Summary (high level):
- VPC layout: 3 subnets (control plane / serving / kv-cache) across 3 AZs; private subnets only.
- Egress: NAT for OS packages, but inference egress must be restricted to Atlas-managed proxies for audit.
- Transit: Transit gateway peering to Atlas TGW with BGP; advertise only private prefixes for the serve subnets.
- Firewall rules: allow TCP 443 inbound from Atlas app tier VLANs to serving LB; allow Redis (6379) and internal RPC ports only from control plane CIDRs.
- KMS: ACM + customer-managed KMS key (we’ll provide Cloud KMS integration guide) — need key policy allowing Redwood service account.
- Ports to request (suggested): 443 (LB), 8443 (health/control plane), 22000 (kv-sync), 6379 (redis), ephemeral 10240-10495 for worker gRPC.
- MTU: keep 9001 for jumbo support if you use ENIs with SR-IOV; otherwise 1500.

Operational notes:
- We recommend prefix-lists for the caches so you can rotate proxies without changing LB rules.
- For HSM/KMS tests we’ll perform a signing roundtrip in staging before go-live.

Next steps:
1) Monica — can you validate the port list against our default firewall baseline?
2) Diane — can your cloud team open the TGW + peering ticket and share the request ID?
3) Once TGW and KMS access are confirmed, we’ll schedule a 60-min architecture walkthrough with infra and security.

I’ve attached a short methods-of-procedure (onboarding-mop.md) with the smoke test steps we’ll run after network connectivity is provisioned.

Thanks — talk soon.

Karthik Iyer
Head of Solutions Engineering
Redwood Inference
Phone: +1 (415) 555-0189

Subject: Re: Private deployment architecture & network gate review

Karthik / Diane — quick follow-up with a couple of clarifying items from the network baseline team. Quoting Diane’s note for context:

> All traffic to the inference cluster must traverse our transit gateway and go through managed NGFW (no public IPs on host NICs).

Questions / asks:
- For the transit path, can you confirm whether Atlas will terminate TLS at the NGFW or if the LB in the serving VPC must terminate TLS? If Atlas terminates, we need a private CA bundle for our health checks to validate.
- For the KV cache (Redis), is high-availability required across AZs (clustered) or is single-az acceptable for initial rollout? Single-AZ will simplify peering but is a lower SLA.
- KMS/HSM: please add the Redwood service account ARN that should be granted decrypt/sign permissions on the CMK; we must record that in the key policy change request.

To keep the ticket minimal, suggested firewall rule text for TGW peering: 
- Source: Atlas App CIDR 10.12.0.0/16
- Destination: Serving LB IP (private)
- Protocol/Ports: TCP/443
- Action: ALLOW

I’ve flagged the suggested port range 10240-10495 as optional — if Atlas prefers a pinned port set we can shrink it.

Will wait for the TGW ticket ID; once we have that we’ll allocate a time window for the smoke tests.

Monica
Network Security, Redwood Inference

From: Diane Brooks <diane.brooks@atlashealth.com>

Thank you — this is great and addresses our ask. A few quick answers:
- Atlas will terminate TLS at the NGFW; we will provide the private CA bundle in the TGW ticket.
- KV cache: we want multi-AZ (clustered) for HA — please include redis-cluster configuration in the MOP.
- KMS: granting Redwood service account arn:aws:iam::123456789012:role/redwood-deploy-access to the CMK is approved; I’ll add this in the key policy request.

I’ve created TGW ticket TGW-2027-5543 and attached the CA bundle in the ticket. Hoping to complete network provisioning by Friday — can we lock a 60-min walkthrough on Friday 16:00 PT? Also sending a DocuSign approval for the onboarding SOW; link below.
